# dumpyard — instructions for LLMs working in this repo

This repo is a static site of pages, notes, PDFs and images. Any folder can have
its own password, and locking `/project-xyz/` covers everything inside it.

Use the `dumpyard` CLI for all changes. Don't edit files in this repo by hand.
If you have the dumpyard skill, follow it; this file covers the same ground.

## Check it works

```sh
dumpyard status        # repo, URL, what's published. No passwords.
```

## Publish

Write the artifact outside this repo, then:

```sh
dumpyard publish report.html --set-password                    # locked, at /report/
dumpyard publish ./project-xyz/ --set-password --expires 7d    # a folder, with expiry
dumpyard publish notes.md --space project-xyz --update         # add to an existing folder
dumpyard publish ./project-xyz/ --replace                      # clear the folder first
```

- **Lock by default.** Publish publicly only when the human says it may be
  public. A mistaken lock is undone with `unlock`; a mistaken public publish
  can't be undone.
- **Add `--expires` only when given a time limit.** Accepted forms: `30m`,
  `12h`, `7d`, `2w`, or a date like `2026-10-01` (UTC). It works only on locked
  folders.
- **Check that it's live.** The link works only if the command exits 0 and ends
  with `Deployed. Live now.` Exit 2 or `NOT DEPLOYED` means nothing is live. Say
  so; don't hand over the link.
- **An existing folder is refused** unless you pass `--update` or `--replace`.
  If you get `already exists`, ask the human which they mean; don't choose.
- **Updating keeps the password.** `--set-password` on a locked folder leaves
  its password alone. `dumpyard lock` on a locked folder rotates it (prints
  `ROTATED`), so run it only when asked.
- **Only folders can be locked.** Put a page that needs its own password into a
  folder of its own.

## What ends up where

- One page published without `--space` is served at `/name/`.
- A folder's own `index.html` is its page and is never overwritten. Without
  one, the folder gets a generated list of its contents.
- `foo.md` is rendered to `/folder/foo`. Start every note with `# Heading`.
  Links: `[[note]]`, `[[note|label]]`, `![[image.png]]`.
- HTML must be self-contained: inline CSS and JS, no external requests.

## Passwords are three words, and can be looked up, so never call one unrecoverable

```sh
dumpyard password /project-xyz/
```

After every publish, give the human:
- the URL the command printed
- the password, if the folder is locked
- the expiry, if one is set
- what is public and what is locked

Locked folders aren't listed on the public index, so the URL is the only way in.

## Don't

- Run `remove` or `prune` unless asked. Both take things offline immediately.
- Link from a public page to a locked one. The build warns when a page does
  this. Fix it; don't leave it.
- Put passwords, tokens or keys in any file or commit message. Giving a
  password to the human in chat is fine.
- Publish credentials or other people's personal data, even behind a password.
